DocsIntro.metaDesc: How Aegisora integrates at the execution boundary: policy, evaluation, enforcement and evidence.
DocsIntro.lead: Aegisora is an execution-control and runtime-governance system for autonomous AI agents. It sits between what an agent proposes and what actually runs in your environment.
DocsIntro.whyP: An agent being able to propose an action does not mean the action should execute. Aegisora evaluates each request against context, policy and risk, then resolves ALLOW, BLOCK or ESCALATE.
DocsIntro.verP: Aegisora did not start as a full runtime. Each release added a layer to the model, from a static rulebook to a closed-loop system with context, risk scoring and durable evidence.

v1.title: The static rulebook
v1.p: The first release matched every agent action against a fixed rulebook. A request either matched an allow-rule or it did not — there was no context, no scoring, no escalation path.
v1.b1: Static YAML rulebooks, evaluated per action name
v1.b2: Binary outcome: match or no match

v2.title: From rules to risk
v2.p: 2.0 introduced context gathering and a risk-scoring layer ahead of the policy check. The outcome stopped being binary: every request now resolves to ALLOW, BLOCK, or ESCALATE.
v2.b2: Caller-supplied risk value evaluated against policy conditions

v3.title: The full runtime
v3.p: Version 3.0 introduced the closed-loop control plane. Eight stages carry every request from intent to consequence, and every decision writes durable, queryable evidence that feeds back into risk.
v3.b2: Decision API called before your agent executes an action
v3.b4: Hash-chained evidence record for every decision
v3.b6: Approvals, incidents and webhooks as first-class objects

v4.title: Continuity Seal
v4.p: Continuity Seal extends runtime governance from authorization into the integrity of the execution itself. The execution must remain the execution that was authorized.
v4.b1: Deterministic execution sealing with immutable seal identity
v4.b4: Tool execution bound to its authorization receipt
v4.b5: sealId correlation across the evidence layer
v4.b6: Blocked execution and effect reconciliation evidence

s1.label: Request
s1.title: The agent proposes an action
s1.body: Before a sensitive tool runs, your application sends the action with its context: the tool, the target and any amount involved.

s2.title: Aegisora checks policy and authority

s3.label: Decide
s3.title: A verdict comes back before execution
s3.body: ALLOW runs the tool. ESCALATE waits for a person. BLOCK stops it. With no matching policy, the default is BLOCK.

s4.label: Record

principle.text: Aegisora answers before the tool runs: the action, the agent, the context and the policy go in, and a verdict with a reason comes out. When nothing matches, nothing runs.

problem.intro: Permissions are often granted once, at setup. A sensitive action needs a decision at the moment it is requested.
problem.badBody: Access is granted once, logs are written after the action ran, and no record a reviewer can verify.
problem.goodBody: A verdict for every sensitive action before it runs, people approve what needs it, evidence is chained.

HomeBody.reveal: Agent actions happen across tools, APIs, databases and inboxes every minute. Aegisora captures each request, decides before it runs, and records proof you can verify, so control keeps up with your agents.
